_comment: The SHAPE of a bench fleet — not a fleet. This file carries the ports a
backend answers on and the one machine every campaign has, the one it runs
on. Your own machines are declared in hosts.local.json, which is not
committed; copy hosts.local.example.json to start one.
The split is not only about credentials. A bench fleet is a description of
one room: these GPUs, that dual boot, a mini PC on a shelf. It is true there
and false everywhere else, so a repository is the wrong place for it —
somebody cloning this harness wants the machinery, never someone else's
hardware. discover.ps1 merges the two on the id: a known id is completed
field by field, an unknown one is simply a new machine.
A machine entry, all fields optional but id:
id              short name, used in results and as the merge key
label           one line for a human; never shown in a shared report
kind            how it is reached: local | ssh | wsl-sshpass | plink
roles           what it can be in a campaign: host, client, or both
perfMeaningful  false on a VM, a machine with no GPU or a software
encoder — the report then never fails it on latency
dualBoot        present when one address answers under two systems; the
TTL of a ping decides which one is up today
expect          what you believe is there, so discover can say 'gone'
rather than silently shrinking the matrix
address         where it lives — hosts.local.json ONLY
user, password  how to log in — hosts.local.json ONLY
sshAlias        an entry of ~/.ssh/config, better than a password
Everything a local file declares is a HINT, never a fact: leases move,
the same address can be two different machines, and a box can be off.
discover.ps1 probes every field it can and writes what it actually found.

ports._comment: The products' own defaults, and probed rather than assumed. Wolf impersonates GameStream and answers on the same pair, so a site running both on one machine rebases one of them — put that, and any other local shift, in the "ports" block of hosts.local.json. A dev instance in particular almost never sits where you expect: read its log or netstat, never the default.
